title: Ashwin Watched the Bowling Changes. That Was When He Knew Gill Had Grown.
excerpt: India's 26-year-old captain managed five bowlers with surgical precision in Mullanpur. On Saturday, he begins the road to the 2027 World Cup without Kohli.
body:
He won the Test by an innings and 300 runs. Three days later, he will lead the same dressing room — minus its most famous name — into an ODI series that begins India's road to the 2027 World Cup. Shubman Gill is 26 years old. He is captaining India in Tests and ODIs simultaneously. And the people who have done both before him are paying attention.

Ravichandran Ashwin, who has played under every Indian captain from Dhoni to Rohit, watched the one-off Test against Afghanistan in Mullanpur and came away impressed by something specific. Not Gill's century — that was expected. The bowling changes.

"His captaincy has come a long way in the last four months," Ashwin said on his YouTube channel. "Manav Suthar gets overspin, which means he won't be as effective as the ball gets old. So Gill used him with the new ball. Then he bowled Kuldeep Yadav with the older ball and used Sundar against the left-handers."

Ashwin went further. "Even in the second innings, when he could have gone back to Suthar with the old ball, he brilliantly went for Siraj and got a breakthrough. He also made Prasidh bowl straighter with a more leg-side field. He used Kuldeep more to help him regain confidence because Kuldeep has had a poor last 18 months. He knows all these bowlers will be important, so he brought them all perfectly into the game."

This is not a young captain still finding his feet. This is preparation.

Former India player Abhishek Nayar, who worked closely with the team as assistant coach, drew a direct comparison. "Very similar to Rohit," Nayar said on Star Sports. "Rohit Sharma was a captain who used to prepare himself a lot. Shubman watches the video of every batter and bowler. He tries to understand how to get them out technically. He makes his own strategies and game plans."

What the ODI series means

On Saturday, June 13, Gill will walk out at Dharamsala for the first ODI against Afghanistan with a squad that looks markedly different from the one that played the 2023 World Cup final. Virat Kohli is injured — a hamstring tear from the IPL final has ruled him out, and Yashasvi Jaiswal has replaced him. Rohit Sharma, cleared fit after his own hamstring trouble during the IPL, returns as an opener rather than captain. Hardik Pandya, back from a back spasm, slots in at No. 6.

The full squad reads: Shubman Gill (C), Rohit Sharma, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shreyas Iyer (VC), KL Rahul, Ishan Kishan, Hardik Pandya, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Prasidh Krishna, Prince Yadav, Gurnoor Brar, Harsh Dubey.

The series runs across three venues — Dharamsala on June 13, Lucknow on June 17, and Chennai on June 20. It is India's first ODI assignment since the 1-2 loss to New Zealand in January. And it is the first step in a schedule that includes six bilateral ODI series and up to 18 ODIs before the 2027 World Cup in South Africa.

The transition is happening

The dynamic inside this dressing room has quietly shifted. Gill is no longer the young batter learning from Rohit and Kohli. He is the captain managing their workloads, deciding their batting positions, and planning a bowling attack that includes two left-arm spinners, a wrist spinner, and three seamers.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZUrG0Zifcg/

For NRI fans who grew up watching Dhoni hand the armband to Kohli, and Kohli to Rohit, this is the next chapter — and it is arriving faster than anyone expected. Gill has now captained nine Tests, winning five. His batting average as captain across formats sits comfortably above 50. And in Mullanpur, he scored 126 and enforced the follow-on on Day 3, wrapping up the match before lunch on the same day.

Ashwin's observation was the most revealing. Gill did not just use five bowlers. He used each one at the right time, for the right batter, with the right ball age. That is not instinct alone. That is homework.

The Afghanistan ODI series is not expected to test India's depth in the way England away will in July. But it will test something else: whether Gill can manage a squad that includes his predecessor as opener, a returning all-rounder who has not played an ODI in 15 months, and a 24-year-old replacement batting at No. 3 for the first time in a bilateral series.

India's 2027 World Cup campaign starts at Dharamsala on Saturday. Gill, at 26, is driving it.
